strengths: Addresses a relevant NLP problem: affordable generation for ten Indian languages, including underserved languages such as Assamese, Konkani, Maithili, Odia, and Sanskrit.

The reported 13–368M-parameter model family explores useful monolingual, bilingual, and multilingual configurations. Several displayed continuations suggest that compact, language-specialized models deserve further investigation.

Culturally grounded prompts and native-speaker judgments are appropriate ingredients for evaluating these models. Providing prompts, example outputs, and the instruction-data composition makes parts of the work inspectable.
weaknesses: The central method is not reproducible from the manuscript. The claimed architectural innovations are unspecified, and Section 4.4, Tokenization, is empty despite the tokenizer being a major contribution. Model configurations, corpus sizes and precise sources, training hyperparameters, optimization schedules, and training duration are missing. Only future API access is promised; no implementation or checkpoint access is provided in the manuscript.

The human evaluation is insufficient to establish the broad superiority claims. Each evaluated language has only four prompts and nominally three generations per prompt. The paper does not adequately specify annotator counts per item, rating rubrics, blinding, agreement, uncertainty, or selection of the 'top-3' outputs. Assigning factuality zero when a premise cannot be verified also conflates unverifiability with falsehood, particularly for fictional continuations.

Result attribution contains serious inconsistencies requiring an audit. The 'I like sweets' outputs attributed to GPT-Neo and GPT2-XL in Table 20 reappear under BLOOM 560M and 1.1B in Table 21; some BLOOM 3B cells instead contain the unrelated 'Our country' prompt. Tables 5 and 12 also reproduce the same Bangla continuations under different Paramanu model sizes. These discrepancies undermine confidence in which outputs support the reported scores.

The comparisons do not isolate the proposed contribution. Most baselines are predominantly English-oriented, and there is no competitive Indic-focused baseline or decoder trained with matched data and compute. ChatGPT was accessed through the web interface, without establishing equivalent conversation context or decoding settings. These experiments cannot substantiate general superiority over contemporary multilingual models.

The explanations for the gains remain untested. There are no controlled ablations of architecture, tokenizer, corpus balancing, or typological grouping. Declining performance across larger BLOOM variants does not demonstrate the curse of multilinguality, since the language set remains unchanged. Tokenizing an unseen language likewise does not establish successful generation in that language. Tokenizer-dependent perplexities in Table 2 do not resolve these questions without comparable evaluation units and adequately documented held-out data.

The efficiency claims exceed the measurements. The conclusion infers a 20–66-fold inference speedup from parameter-count ratios. Table 11 contains no baseline timings and omits CPU specifications, runtime, threading, and workload details. Training on one GPU establishes a hardware requirement, but does not establish low total training cost without GPU-hours and processed-token counts.

Evidence for the remaining languages and instruction-tuned capabilities is largely illustrative rather than a held-out evaluation. Some demonstrations contradict their favorable interpretation: Figure 24 answers a question about African governments improving air connectivity with road-safety advice. Training–evaluation overlap is not assessed. A documented implementation, an audit of output attribution, and a substantially redesigned evaluation are needed before the work meets Findings' soundness and reproducibility threshold; this warrants resubmission after substantial work.
